preamble: Debuccalization of the alveolar fricative [s] to a glottal stop [ʔ] removes the oral constriction and leaves only glottal closure. Most Caribbean and other lowland Spanish dialects weaken coda /s/ to [h] or delete it, but Puerto Rican Spanish has also developed a glottal-stop variant of word-final /s/. It was first described between vowels (las alas) and later found before consonants and pauses as well; a Lancaster, Pennsylvania study found it among Puerto Rican speakers but not among Cuban or Dominican speakers. A historical parallel occurs in Kuki-Chin (Tibeto-Burman): the Proto-Sino-Tibetan suffix *-s became the final glottal stop of Proto-Kuki-Chin, which Mizo writes with final ⟨h⟩, as in hnih 'two' and sarih 'seven'.

examples.note: Word-final /s/ before a vowel, the context where the glottal variant was first described (Mohamed & Muntendam 2020)
